extracted.intended_audience: Federal agency rulewriters, agency heads, OMB/OIRA staff, regulatory policy advisors, and other executive-branch regulatory officials
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory procedures for federal agencies on planning, drafting, reviewing, and publishing regulations under Executive Order 12866, including principles for regulation, centralized OIRA review, planning documents, public participation, and disclosure requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Philosophy (general standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies should promulgate only such regulations as are required by law, are necessary to interpret the law, or are made necessary by compelling public need; agencies should assess all costs and benefits of available regulatory alternatives, including the alternative of not regulating; costs and benefits include both quantifiable and qualitative measures; agencies should select approaches that maximize net benefits unless a statute requires another approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider quantifiable and non‑quantifiable costs/benefits; evaluate the option of not regulating; choose the alternative that maximizes net benefits (economic, environmental, public health/safety, distributive impacts, equity) unless statute dictates otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 1: Identify the problem and assess its significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall identify the problem it intends to address (including market or institutional failures) and assess the significance of that problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the market/institutional failure motivating action and provide an assessment of how significant the problem is within the agency's jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 2: Examine whether existing law/regulations contribute to the problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall examine whether existing regulations (or other law) have created, or contributed to, the problem and whether those regulations should be modified to achieve the regulatory goal more effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze current rules for unintended effects and consider modifying or replacing existing requirements rather than adding new, duplicative ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 3: Identify and assess alternatives to direct regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall identify and assess available alternatives to direct regulation, including economic incentives (user fees, marketable permits) or providing information to enable private choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate non‑regulatory and incentive‑based approaches and compare them to direct regulatory approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 4: Consider the degree and nature of risks in priority setting
rubrics_metrics.description: In setting regulatory priorities, agencies shall consider, to the extent reasonable, the degree and nature of risks posed by various substances or activities within their jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use risk characterization to inform prioritization of regulatory actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 5: Design cost‑effective regulations considering innovation and other factors
rubrics_metrics.description: When regulation is the best method, agencies shall design regulations in the most cost‑effective manner, considering incentives for innovation, consistency, predictability, enforcement and compliance costs, flexibility, distributive impacts, and equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select regulatory designs that achieve objectives at least cost and that promote innovation, predictability, and fair distribution of impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 6: Reasoned determination that benefits justify costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall assess both costs and benefits of the intended regulation and, recognizing that some are hard to quantify, adopt a regulation only upon a reasoned determination that benefits justify its costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a documented, reasoned justification demonstrating net benefits (including qualitative considerations where quantification is infeasible).

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 7: Base decisions on best reasonably obtainable information
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall base its decisions on the best reasonably obtainable scientific, technical, economic, and other information concerning the need for, and consequences of, the intended regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use best available evidence and document data sources, methods, and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 8: Specify performance objectives where feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall identify and assess alternative forms of regulation and, to the extent feasible, specify performance objectives rather than prescribing specific behavior or manner of compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor outcome‑based/performance standards that allow regulated parties flexibility in how they comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 9: Seek views and minimize unique burdens on state/local/tribal governments
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherever feasible agencies shall seek views of appropriate State, local, and tribal officials before imposing regulatory requirements that might significantly or uniquely affect them, assess effects on these governments (including resource availability), and seek to minimize unique burdens while achieving objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage sub‑federal governments early; assess federalism impacts and harmonize federal and non‑federal requirements where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 10: Avoid inconsistent, incompatible, or duplicative regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall avoid regulations that are inconsistent, incompatible, or duplicative with its other regulations or those of other Federal agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate across agencies and review existing regulatory landscape to prevent overlap or conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 11: Tailor regulations to impose the least burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall tailor its regulations to impose the least burden on society, including individuals and businesses of differing sizes, consistent with obtaining regulatory objectives, taking into account cumulative costs where practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider differential burdens (e.g., small businesses, small communities) and cumulative regulatory costs when designing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 12: Draft rules to be simple and easy to understand
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall draft its regulations to be simple and easy to understand, with the goal of minimizing uncertainty and litigation arising from such uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear, plain language and minimize ambiguity to reduce compliance costs and litigation risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'Regulation'/'Rule' and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'regulation' or 'rule' is an agency statement of general applicability and future effect intended to have the force of law to implement, interpret, or prescribe law or policy or describe procedure/practice requirements; excludes certain categories (formal rulemaking under 5 U.S.C. 556,557; military/foreign affairs functions except procurement/import/export non‑defense; agency organization/personnel; other categories exempted by OIRA Administrator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition to determine whether action is subject to EO 12866 procedures and OIRA review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'Regulatory action' (scope of actions covered)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory action means any substantive action by an agency normally published in the Federal Register that promulgates or is expected to lead to a final rule, including notices of inquiry, advance notices of proposed rulemaking, and notices of proposed rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include early‑stage documents (notices of inquiry, ANPRMs) in planning and potential OIRA review determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'Significant regulatory action'
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'significant regulatory action' is any regulatory action likely to result in a rule that may: (1) Have annual effect on the economy of $100 million or more or adversely affect in a material way the economy/sector/productivity/competition/jobs/environment/public health or State/local/tribal governments; (2) create serious inconsistency or interfere with another agency action; (3) materially alter budgetary impact of entitlements/grants/user fees/loan programs or rights and obligations of recipients; or (4) raise novel legal or policy issues arising out of legal mandates, the President's priorities, or EO principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these threshold tests to identify matters subject to heightened OIRA review and reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual planning: Unified Regulatory Agenda requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall prepare an agenda of all regulations under development or review (Unified Regulatory Agenda) in a manner and time specified by the OIRA Administrator; each regulatory action description must include at minimum an identifier number, a brief summary, legal authority, any legal deadline, and a knowledgeable agency official's name and telephone number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include required metadata for each action so the public, Congress, and other agencies can track planned rulemaking and contact agency officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Plan: content and submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall prepare a Regulatory Plan of its most important significant regulatory actions (approved personally by the agency head) and include at minimum: (A) statement of objectives/priorities and relation to President's priorities; (B) summary of each planned significant action including alternatives and preliminary cost/benefit estimates; (C) summary of legal basis including statutory/court deadlines; (D) statement of need and how action will reduce risks and relate to other risks; (E) schedule for action including deadlines; (F) contact information for public inquiries. Agencies must forward the Plan to OIRA by June 1 each year and Plans are published in the October Unified Regulatory Agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory Plans must be agency‑head–approved, timely submitted, include alternatives and preliminary CBA, and be published for public transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency Policy Meeting and annual coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Early each year's planning cycle the Vice President shall convene a meeting of the Advisors and agency heads to seek common understanding of priorities and coordinate regulatory efforts for the upcoming year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participate in cross‑agency priority setting to align planned regulations with presidential and interagency priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Working Group and interagency coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: OIRA Administrator shall convene a Regulatory Working Group of representatives of agencies with significant domestic regulatory responsibility, Advisors, and the Vice President to assist agencies in identifying/analyzing important regulatory issues, develop innovative techniques, consider comparative risk assessment, and develop streamlined approaches for small businesses; the Working Group shall meet at least quarterly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Working Group as a forum for methodological development, interagency problem solving, and periodic reporting to the Vice President.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation and conferences with state/local/tribal and stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: OIRA Administrator shall meet quarterly with State, local, and tribal representatives to identify regulations that may uniquely or significantly affect them and shall convene conferences with businesses, NGOs, and the public as needed to discuss regulatory issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hold periodic stakeholder consultations to identify burdens and conflicts and to inform regulatory planning and review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of existing regulations (retrospective review program)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 90 days each agency shall submit to OIRA a program under which it will periodically review its existing significant regulations to determine whether any should be modified or eliminated to make the regulatory program more effective, less burdensome, or better aligned with Presidential principles; include significant regulations selected for review in the agency's annual Plan and identify legislative mandates the agency believes are unnecessary or outdated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish and publish a periodic retrospective review program; solicit assistance from state/local/tribal governments to identify burdensome or outdated regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation and comment period (agency responsibilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall provide the public with meaningful participation in the regulatory process; before issuing a NPRM, agencies should seek involvement of those who will benefit or be burdened (including state/local/tribal officials); agencies should afford a meaningful opportunity to comment, which in most cases should include a comment period of not less than 60 days; agencies should explore negotiated rulemaking and consensual mechanisms where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for early stakeholder engagement and typically provide at least 60 days for public comment on proposed rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of Regulatory Policy Officer (RPO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days each agency head shall designate a Regulatory Policy Officer who reports to the agency head and is involved at each stage of the regulatory process to foster effective, innovative, and least‑burdensome regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure RPO participates across rulemaking stages to apply EO principles and coordinate with OIRA as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency submission to OIRA for significant regulatory actions
rubrics_metrics.description: For each matter identified as significant (or determined by OIRA to be significant), the agency shall provide to OIRA: (i) the text of the draft regulatory action with a reasonably detailed description of the need and explanation of how the action meets that need; and (ii) an assessment of potential costs and benefits, including an explanation of consistency with statutory mandate and how it promotes Presidential priorities and avoids undue interference with state/local/tribal governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and submit draft text plus detailed need justification and a costs/benefits assessment for OIRA review of significant actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional analytic requirements for high‑impact significant actions
rubrics_metrics.description: For significant regulatory actions within the scope of section 3(f)(1) (e.g., actions likely to have annual economic effect of $100M+), agencies must provide to OIRA: (i) assessment and underlying analysis of anticipated benefits, with quantification where feasible; (ii) assessment and underlying analysis of anticipated costs, with quantification where feasible (including government and private compliance costs and adverse economic effects); and (iii) assessment and underlying analysis of costs and benefits of potentially effective and reasonably feasible alternatives (including improving current regulation and viable nonregulatory actions), and explanation why the planned action is preferable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide underlying analytical documentation (models, data, assumptions) supporting quantified and qualitative cost/benefit estimates and alternatives comparisons; this is expected for actions meeting the high‑impact threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency and statutory‑deadline exceptions to review procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: In emergency situations or when law obligates faster action, the agency shall notify OIRA as soon as possible and, to the extent practicable, comply with submission requirements; agencies with statutory or court deadlines should schedule proceedings to permit sufficient time for OIRA review where practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If expedited, still notify OIRA promptly and provide as much analytic material as possible under the time constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑publication transparency obligations (agency)
rubrics_metrics.description: After publication or issuance, the agency shall: (i) make available to the public the information submitted to OIRA (per subsections a(3)(B) and (C)); (ii) identify, in a complete, clear, and simple manner, substantive changes between the draft submitted to OIRA and the action announced; and (iii) identify changes made at the suggestion or recommendation of OIRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish supporting analyses and a clear summary of substantive changes and OIRA's role to promote transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language requirement for agency public materials
rubrics_metrics.description: All information provided to the public by the agency shall be in plain, understandable language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure public documents (summaries, explanations, notices) use clear, non‑technical language to be accessible to a broad audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA scope of review (limitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: OIRA may review only actions identified by the agency or identified by OIRA as significant under subsection (a)(3)(A), except as otherwise provided or waived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should designate which planned actions they consider significant; OIRA can reclassify or notify agency that it deems an action significant within 10 working days of receiving the agency's list.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA review timelines and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: OIRA shall waive review or notify the agency in writing within: (A) 10 working days for notices of inquiry, ANPRMs, or other preliminary actions prior to an NPRM; (B) 90 calendar days for all other regulatory actions after submission of required materials (or 45 days if previously reviewed and facts unchanged); (C) review may be extended once by up to 30 calendar days with written Director approval and at the agency head's request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan rulemaking schedules to accommodate OIRA review timeframes and allow for one possible extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA returns and explanation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If OIRA returns a regulatory action to an agency for further consideration of some or all provisions, the Administrator shall provide a written explanation setting forth the pertinent provision of the Executive order on which OIRA is relying; the agency head may respond in writing if they disagree with the return bases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect documented reasons for returns and an opportunity for written agency response; maintain record of disagreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA disclosure rules for communications (oral & written)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the Administrator of OIRA (or a particular designee) shall receive oral communications initiated by persons not employed by the executive branch regarding substance of a regulatory action under review; all substantive communications between OIRA personnel and persons not employed by the executive branch shall: (i) invite an issuing‑agency representative to any meeting; (ii) result in OIRA forwarding to the issuing agency, within 10 working days, all written communications and dates/names of individuals involved in substantive oral communications; and (iii) be publicly disclosed as set out in subsection (b)(4)(C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public and external stakeholders' communications with OIRA are logged and forwarded to agencies; agency reps should attend meetings or request records be forwarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA public log and document disclosure obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: OIRA shall maintain a publicly available log containing at minimum: status of regulatory actions (including Vice Presidential/Presidential consideration requests and decision makers), notations of written communications forwarded to agencies, and dates/names/subjects of substantive oral communications between OIRA personnel and non‑executive‑branch persons; after publication or decision not to publish, OIRA shall make available to the public all documents exchanged between OIRA and the agency during review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIRA must maintain and publish a searchable log and release exchanged documents post‑decision to ensure openness and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language requirement for OIRA public materials
rubrics_metrics.description: All information provided to the public by OIRA shall be in plain, understandable language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIRA must present logs, explanations, and disclosed materials in accessible language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution of interagency conflicts via President/Vice President
rubrics_metrics.description: Disagreements among agency heads or between OMB and an agency that cannot be resolved by the Administrator of OIRA shall be resolved by the President, or the Vice President at the President's request; Vice Presidential/Presidential consideration may be initiated only by the Director, the issuing agency head, or by another agency head with significant interest; the recommendation process shall be concluded within 60 days after review is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use established channels (Director, agency head) to escalate unresolved conflicts; expect a documented VP/President review with 60‑day target.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written submission requirement during VP/Presidential review
rubrics_metrics.description: During Vice Presidential/Presidential review, communications with persons not employed by the Federal Government relating to the substance of the regulatory action and directed to the Advisors or their staffs or to the Vice President's staff shall be in writing and forwarded by the recipient to affected agency(ies) for inclusion in the public docket; if not in writing, staff shall inform the outside party that the matter is under review and request written comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External parties should submit written communications during high‑level review; agencies will include such submissions in the public docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication restriction pending OIRA review completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as required by law, an agency shall not publish or otherwise issue any regulatory action subject to section 6 review until (1) OIRA notifies the agency that it has waived review or completed review without requests for further consideration, or (2) the applicable time period in section 6(b)(2) expires without OIRA returning the action for further consideration, unless the agency requests Presidential consideration through the Vice President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not publish significant regulatory actions until OIRA review is complete or its time limit lapses, unless the agency requests Presidential consideration per section 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency authority preserved
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the order shall be construed as displacing the agencies' authority or responsibilities as authorized by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EO 12866 governs planning/review/coordination but does not change statutory agency authorities or responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review/rights preserved (management only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this Executive order affects otherwise available judicial review of agency action; the order is intended to improve internal management and does not create enforceable rights or benefits against the U.S. or its agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EO creates internal procedures and transparency obligations but does not create private legal causes of action.
